basis: Familial hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, with possible ventricular noncompaction, directly affects myocardium.
Marrow failure and the diagnostic nail/skin/oral leukoplakia triad define DC/TBD; pulmonary and hepatic injury vary and are not established in >=30% across this umbrella.
Glycosylation disorder with developmental impairment; strabismus and persistent GI dysfunction/reflux each occur in 80-99%; skeletal and renal anomalies are occasional.
Malignancy of the fallopian tube, a reproductive organ outside the axes; no common direct injury to another axis established.
Disease of the pupil and iris.
Skeletal dysplasia with short bones, joint stiffness and hip dysplasia; damaging ocular, cardiac and respiratory findings are subtype dependent across this umbrella.
Malignant germ cell tumor arising in the ovary; reproductive tumor origin does not establish endocrine gland dysfunction.
Pressure causes skin and subcutaneous tissue necrosis; deeper muscle or bone destruction is confined to advanced ulcers.
Lysosomal storage disorder causing progressive neuronal degeneration, dementia and seizures; retinal degeneration is not characteristic of adult Kufs disease.
Primary intraosseous sarcoma directly occupies and destroys bone.
Syndromic intellectual disability; hip dislocation, clubfoot and kyphosis occur in 30-79%, as does strabismus. Recurrent infections do not establish lasting lung damage.
Growth hormone-secreting pituitary endocrine neoplasm; no common direct damage to another axis established by the supplied phenotypes.
Hereditary primary glaucoma directly damages the eye and optic nerve.
Bacterial, immune-mediated periodontal destruction; alveolar bone loss is a defining diagnostic feature, accompanying rapid attachment and tooth loss.
Inherited cardiac repolarization disorder causing ventricular arrhythmias; syncope does not establish primary neurologic injury.
Sandfly-transmitted viral infection; usual fever and influenza-like symptoms do not establish lasting organ damage.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and brachydactyly type E define the haploinsufficiency syndrome; short stature and obesity alone do not establish additional organ injury.
ACTH pituitary tumor usually causes cortisol excess; myopathy/bone loss occur in roughly 50-80% and persistent skin atrophy/bruising in >50%; silent tumors are a minority.
Hereditary anomaly of sebaceous glands, which are skin appendages rather than endocrine glands.
Developmental brain and persistent skin abnormalities define the syndrome; exotropia occurs in 4/4. Hypermobility/weakness in 2/4 do not establish intrinsic muscle or joint damage.
Rhabdoid malignancy arising in and directly occupying the kidney.
Inflammation directly affects the colon; this umbrella includes ischemic and chemical causes, so an infectious or immune mechanism is not universal.
Malignant ovarian teratoma with thyroid-type tissue; reproductive tumor origin has no axis. Thyrotoxicosis is uncommon and does not justify an endocrine label.
Asthma defines immune-mediated airway disease; short stature and elevated circulating IgA alone do not establish skeletal damage or another organ disorder.
Inherited transverse groove of external nasal skin; no evidence of nasal airway disease.
